symptom: A project script with `alter module X add jar dependency (group=…, artifact=…, version=…)` cannot be executed twice: the second exec fails with "jar dependency 'g:a' already exists in module 'X'; use SET to update version" and stops there, and the suggested `set jar dependency … version` fails on a fresh project where the coordinate is absent, so no single statement is re-runnable.
cause: The IF NOT EXISTS family (ADD ATTRIBUTE, ADD VALUE, ADD INDEX, CREATE ENTITY …) had never reached `alterModuleJarDepAction`. Added `ADD JAR DEPENDENCY ifNotExists? (…)`, carried as `AddJarDepAction.IfNotExists`; `applyJarDepAction` now returns a skip notice instead of the error when the guard is set, and `execAlterModuleJarDep` writes nothing and reports Unchanged when every action skipped (otherwise `ReportMutation`, so a restated SET … VERSION also says Unchanged).
insight: Match the precedent's semantics, not the issue's wish list: every IF NOT EXISTS form leaves the stored element untouched, so a present coordinate with ANOTHER version is skipped too — but a silent skip would let a version bump in the script never reach the model, so the notice names the stored version and the exact `set jar dependency … version` to run. An upsert spelling was not needed: guarded ADD + SET … VERSION is already a re-runnable pair, because storage elides the restated SET (ADR-0008). Because check replays exec's own `applyJarDepAction`, giving it the skip made `check -p` agree for free — changing its signature is what kept the two from drifting. Verified on a copy of an 11.16 project by md5 of every project file: run 1 changes the module-settings .mxunit and the .mpr; runs 2 (same version) and 3 (other version) change 0 files and leave the unit's mtime alone; the bare ADD still refuses.
test: mdl/visitor/jar_dependency_if_not_exists_test.go; mdl/executor/jar_dependency_if_not_exists_test.go (mock, PedApp rerun file hashes, check/exec agreement)
